title: ZTIE-Issues — Repository Structure Map
intro: The **REPO FACTS** sections are generated from the git tree and are authoritative. The **INTERPRETATION** section applies the ZTIE phase/node framing. Every annotated path is validated against the real tree, so a renamed or removed directory surfaces as a drift warning instead of silently misleading a reader.

roles.lambdas/intake: P1 — API Gateway intake receiver (Forensic). Thin lambda: handler + tests only, no awsio/pure module.
roles.lambdas/detonation: P2 — dynamic/behavioral lane (ephemeral EC2, host-native SSM)
roles.lambdas/hub_ingest: RD-013 boundary — Hub-side validating ingestion gate (fail-closed, allow-list)
roles.lambdas/hub_synthesize: P3 — synthesis / convergence of static + dynamic evidence
roles.lambdas/hub_verdict: P3 — advisory verdict derivation (RD-040, never auto-acted)
roles.lambdas/pde_handoff: P4 — ACCEPT → push hash-verified artifact Forensic→Pipeline-Sandbox (RD-047)
roles.lambdas/pde_reject: P4 — REJECT → destroy artifact + chamber in Forensic
roles.docs/governance: Govern layer — sequencing, operating model, work log, reusable-OS separation
roles.docs/session-briefs: Per-story AI/human handoff records (brief + PROMPT pairs, on-deck pointer)
roles.lib/decision_auth: Shared crypto lib — offline Hub-signed decision-token verification (RD-048/049)
roles.infra/lib: CDK v2 TypeScript stacks (11 stacks across 3 AWS accounts)

groups.label: Phase 2 — Detonation lanes (Forensic)
groups.note: Static and dynamic lanes run concurrently under a Step Functions parallel fork; the collector joins them.

groups.label: RD-013 boundary — the one hard Forensic→Hub gate
groups.note: Not a numbered phase. hub_ingest is the fail-closed validating gate; only bounded, derived, verdict-free data crosses.

footer:
**Three-account topology:** Pipeline-Hub `641628980935` (control plane) · Forensic `360999005254` (blast zone / detonation) · Pipeline-Sandbox `586917955591` (PDE landing). **Split-brain workflow:** Gemini plans (architecture, sequencing, validation packages); Kiro executes one story per session. The RUNBOOK master table is the source of truth for what's next.

> ⚠️ Note the distinction: the top-level `dashboard/` directory is the **static SPA** (HTML/CSS/JS); `lambdas/hub_dashboard/` is the **Hub lambda that serves its JSON payload**. They are different things.
